BackstoryDef.title: sandcrawler-born
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was born between the third and fourth deck of a moving fortress and teethed on a hydrospanner. Home was engine-warmth, kin in every hammock, and the endless sorting of salvage into treasure and slag. [PAWN_pronoun] can sleep through any machine noise and through no silence at all.

BackstoryDef.title: tinkerer's child
BackstoryDef.description: Other children were given toys. [PAWN_nameDef] was given broken things and a promise: fix it and it is yours. By ten [PAWN_pronoun] owned a small kingdom of resurrected machines, and one prized wreck [PAWN_pronoun] never managed to wake — carried from camp to camp, just in case.

BackstoryDef.title: bazaar haggler
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] worked the sand bazaars where everything is for sale twice and warranty is a word for tourists. [PAWN_pronoun] can price a droid by the sound of its servos and a customer by the way they hold their credits, and considers a deal where only one side is happy to be sloppy work.

BackstoryDef.title: salvage master
BackstoryDef.description: Where others see a wreck, [PAWN_nameDef] sees an inventory. [PAWN_pronoun] led recovery crews onto crashed freighters, dead war machines and buried ruins, and lives by the scavenger's creed: nothing is garbage, some things are merely patient.

BackstoryDef.title: moot speaker
BackstoryDef.description: When the clans gather to divide territory, settle feuds and set the season's prices, someone must hold the floor. [PAWN_nameDef] held it for years — part judge, part auctioneer, part storyteller — and learned that a fair split everyone grumbles about is the only kind that lasts.

BackstoryDef.title: spring-sworn
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was raised at the covenant pools, where the mist off the cool springs is the closest this planet comes to mercy. [PAWN_pronoun] was taught to name every living thing in the freehold and what each owes the others — and that a person is just one more strand in that weave, no more and no less.

BackstoryDef.title: drought-marked
BackstoryDef.description: The year the spring failed, [PAWN_nameDef] watched the green die in order: first the tender things, then the tough ones, then the animals that ate them. The clan survived on stored water and harder arithmetic. [PAWN_pronoun] wastes nothing now, and never quite trusts a full cistern.

BackstoryDef.title: web-tender
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] kept the Green Oath: heal what can be healed, plant what was taken, and kill nothing that has kin. [PAWN_pronoun] knows soil, root-rot, grafting and the diseases of every creature the freeholds shelter — and will bind a stranger's wounds with the same hands that refuse to hold a hunter's rifle.

BackstoryDef.title: seed-carrier
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] walked between the freeholds with a satchel of seeds and cuttings, planting shade and forage along every route [PAWN_pronoun] traveled. Some of those trees are older than the settlements they now cool. [PAWN_pronoun] measures a life by what grows behind it.

BackstoryDef.title: freehold warrior
BackstoryDef.description: The clans do not march to war; they make war out of coming to them. [PAWN_nameDef] fought from tree-line and irrigation ditch, defending ground [PAWN_pronoun] had personally planted, and was devastating there — and half a person anywhere else. Ask [PAWN_objective] to raid across open sand and you will learn the difference.

BackstoryDef.title: casket-cradled
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in a yard where the honored elders were two meters of welded plate with a person somewhere inside. [PAWN_pronoun] carried their oil, learned their muffled voices, and never once found them frightening. Everyone [PAWN_pronoun] loved most had already given their body to the iron.

BackstoryDef.title: scrap-sifter
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] worked the junk mountains barefoot, sorting fast for the crew boss and faster for [PAWN_possessive] own pockets. [PAWN_pronoun] learned metal by taste of the air around it, and learned early that everything valuable is heavy, sharp, or already claimed by someone bigger.

BackstoryDef.title: casket-wright
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] built and maintained the clan's warcaskets — cutting failed flesh away from steel, welding new armor over old scars, hearing confession through a speaker grille while elbow-deep in someone's life support. Nothing about a body surprises or upsets [PAWN_objective] anymore. Nothing at all.

BackstoryDef.title: casket-denied
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] volunteered for the iron and the wrights refused [PAWN_objective] — wrong blood, wrong nerves, wrong luck. [PAWN_pronoun] has worked twice as hard as everyone since, as if enough labor could re-open the question. It could not, and [PAWN_pronoun] knows it, and [PAWN_pronoun] keeps working anyway.

BackstoryDef.title: wall-of-meat veteran
BackstoryDef.description: Junker doctrine is simple: the caskets anchor the line and the unarmored hold the gaps between them. [PAWN_nameDef] held a gap. Several times. [PAWN_pronoun] fights best shoulder-to-shoulder with something enormous, and has the survivor's habit of counting exits in every room.

BackstoryDef.title: shore-rat
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up skimming the terminator seas for anything that hadn't rotted yet — fuel slick, drowned scrap, the occasional body. [PAWN_pronoun] learned early that the tide gives less than it takes, and never expected much from anything since.

BackstoryDef.title: still-master
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] runs a distillation stack that turns the terminator sea's rot into fuel a caravan can burn. [PAWN_pronoun] can smell a bad batch from across the room and has never once let a still stand cold while there was slick left to crack.

BackstoryDef.title: pipe-tapper
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] walked the Free Droid Enclaves' fuel lines end to end, tapping what the Junkers needed and patching what [PAWN_pronoun] tapped so nobody downstream noticed the loss. The FDE droids that keep count are not fooled, and they do not forget a tapper's face.
